seal.statement: A failed push gate, by any path, keeps the evidence that names its failure. The acceptance runner buffers every command's output into a captured artifact inside the gate checkout (spawnSync, piped), so the change proof's per-file results never reach the terminal, and gateExactSha (scripts/checks/push-gate-corpus-worktree.js, added by d9819d43e) removes that checkout on every exit; the publisher already keeps a failed gate's receipt and first failing artifact (retainGateDiagnostics, fc6db88ee, after the 2026-08-19 incident) and the direct-push gate regressed that class. Now: gateExactSha keeps the same diagnostics, through the publisher's one retainGateDiagnostics, on every non-zero return (a failed run, a replaced injection link, a dirtied checkout) before the checkout is removed, and prints where; the run summary names the failing test files of the first failing command from its captured artifact, read line by line through the bounded reader (the runner's file-level verdict lines only, the last verdict deciding, a retried-once pass green, lab-relayed lines read), bounded with an explicit withheld count and saying 'summary line absent - list may be incomplete' instead of a count when no runner summary line was captured; the verdict stays the command's status; and the pre-push banner says what actually happens.

Relay shapes and the denominator (brief item 5 and item 2). Measured from the code: the change proof runs the classified runner (push-gate-change-proof.js -> run-classified-test-files.js), which runs run-test-files.js once per lane batch of at most 100 files with stdio inherit, so a change proof's stdout carries ONE '# test-files ... fail=N' line PER BATCH, not one; when placed across the lab, each lab machine's lines are relayed after the controller's own files as '[machine] <line>' (relayShardLines), and every file red there is rerun on the controller, whose new column-0 verdict decides it. A strict '^not ok <path> \(' match therefore misses lab-red files that were never rerun (over the 20-file rerun cap), and 'the final # test-files line' is only the last batch's figure. Decision: the summary reads the runner's own line shapes from one owner (TEST_FILE_LINE in run-test-files.js; probe.js's duplicate regexes now import it), strips the relay prefix through one owner (RELAYED_LINE_PREFIX, exported beside the one relayedLine producer in probe.js), decides each file by its LAST verdict line, counts a '# retried-once pass' as green, and prints the count of failing files it named; the runner's summary lines are used as the completeness signal (none captured -> 'summary line absent - list may be incomplete' and no count), together with a signal-ended command and any truncated line that may be a file verdict (a line longer than the bounded reader's 256-byte prefix; the longest test path is 115 bytes). Summing fail= across summary lines was rejected as the count: placed reruns and retried files are counted twice. The captured artifact stored stdout as one JSON string, i.e. one physical line of up to 64 MB, which no line reader can use; the artifact now stores stdoutLines/stderrLines (one JSON string per physical line, schemaVersion 2) and is read through readBoundedOutput's onLinePrefix - never JSON.parse of the document. No code reads the artifact's stdout field (grep: only humans; the publisher test fixture writes its own). Witness (c) carries a relayed lab-red, a lab-red decided green on the controller, nested 'not ok N -' TAP lines and a lookalike.

Signal path. gateExactSha's signal handlers (SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP) now release the checkout through the same releaseCheckout as finally, with the conventional 128+n status, so an interrupted gate retains whatever exists before removing the checkout. In practice: the gate runs the hook with spawnSync, which blocks the event loop, so a handler cannot run until the child returns. A terminal Ctrl-C reaches the hook's process group too; the child dies, spawnSync returns with status null, runInExactCheckout returns failure and finally retains then removes - the handler fires afterwards on an already-removed checkout (removeWorktree then is a reported no-op). A SIGTERM sent to the gate process alone waits for the hook to finish. And the acceptance runner writes its report only after its last command, so an interrupted run usually has no report and retention prints '[push-gate] no acceptance receipt to retain from the gate checkout; the output above is all the gate left' - stated, not silent.

gateExactSha split into gateExactSha + runInExactCheckout; one status flag (initialised to failure, so a throw retains too) decides in finally, and the signal handlers call the same releaseCheckout, which on any non-zero status calls the publisher's retainGateDiagnostics (now exported; no second implementation) and prints '[push-gate] gate diagnostics retained in <dir>' or that there was nothing to retain, then removes the checkout. Acceptance runner: the captured artifact stores stdoutLines/stderrLines (schemaVersion 2, one JSON string per physical line) and exports readCapturedStdout, which reads it through run-test-files' readBoundedOutput (onLinePrefix), never JSON.parse of the document. run-test-files.js owns TEST_FILE_LINE (verdict, retried-once pass, summary line shapes; probe.js's duplicate regexes now import it) and testFileVerdictReader (last verdict decides, retried pass green, summary lines counted). probe.js owns the relay shape (relayedLine producer + exported RELAYED_LINE_PREFIX). renderRunSummary(run, root) appends, for the first failing command, 'failing test files: N' (or 'summary line absent - list may be incomplete' / 'the command ended by SIGx - ...' / 'N verdict line(s) too long to read - ...' instead of N), at most 20 files, and '... - C throw before any report (--ref-lines missing): exit=1, "[push-gate] no acceptance receipt to retain ...", original ENOENT still printed.
- D no report, exit 1: exit=1, "no acceptance receipt to retain". Truthful.
- E report names an artifact that does not exist: exit=1, the report IS copied (kept: g.report.json) but the gate prints "no acceptance receipt to retain from the gate checkout" - a false line (retainGateDiagnostics returns null after copying the report; publish-head.js:404-430). - G SIGTERM to the gate pid alone, child exits 1: exit=1, retained. H same, child exits 0: exit=0, nothing retained - the signal is swallowed. Pre-existing: base ec63fbb00 gives exit=0 too (p1base). I Ctrl-C to the process group: exit=1 (not 130), retained, checkout removed. J SIGKILL: no retention, checkout stranded (unavoidable).
- The signal handler (push-gate-corpus-worktree.js:248-262) can never run: gateExactSha is wholly synchronous and finally removes the handlers before the event loop turns (G/H/I exit codes prove it; exit is never 128+n). The edit to it is dead code and the log's "the handler fires afterwards" is wrong. Pre-existing, non-blocking; deleting the handler would shrink scripts/.

Correction (R21: the 2026-10-03T14:19:42.310Z entry is not edited, this supersedes its claim). That entry says gateExactSha's signal handler 'fires afterwards on an already-removed checkout'. It does not: gateExactSha is wholly synchronous (spawnSync), and its finally removes the listeners before the event loop ever turns, so no handler runs during a gate (verifier probes G/H/I: the exit is never 128+n). The first attempt's edit routing the handler through releaseCheckout was dead code and is removed; removeWorktreeOnSignal is back to its ec63fbb00 form. The handler is not inert, though: while installed it replaces Node's default signal action, which is exactly why a SIGTERM sent to the gate process alone during spawnSync is swallowed (next finding). Process note: solve v2 has no 'continue' verb (usage: start|note|probe|land|evidence|board), so this corrective attempt is recorded with 'note --attempt' after the bound rejection.

For the owner of scripts/checks/push-gate-corpus-worktree.js, NOT fixed here (pre-existing on ec63fbb00, verifier p1base): (1) a SIGTERM sent to the gate process alone is swallowed - exit 0 with a passing child, nothing retained - because the cleanup listeners installed around the synchronous spawnSync replace the default action and are removed before the loop turns; the fix belongs to the gate's signal design (honour a signal that arrived during spawnSync, or do not install listeners on the synchronous path), with its own witness. (2) Found while writing the throw witness: a gate command that deletes the checkout's .git link exits 0 when the gate checkout lives inside the repository (test-output/push-gate-worktrees/...): the dirty check's git status falls through to the enclosing repository and reports it clean. The throw witness therefore points .git at a nonexistent gitdir instead. Both are mutation-check holes of the dirty/signal owner, not of retention.

Such a line cannot hide incompleteness: completeness is decided from summary totals against plan lines, not from the count of distinct named files. The verifier's other residual - a non-test command printing 'failing test files: summary line absent - list may be incomplete' - is fixed: the list is attempted only when a test runner spoke in the command's stdout (a verdict, summary, plan or signalled-batch line, or an unread verdict head); witnessed.

C1 class census - every way the change proof's runner can stop or skip files without a per-file verdict, and how the summary now knows. Completeness is derived positively: runClassifiedTestFiles writes '# test-files planned=N' (its whole input) before any batch, every run-test-files batch ends with '# test-files total=n ...', and the list is called complete only when the summed totals cover the summed plans, no command or batch ended by a signal, and every verdict line was read whole; with no plan line (a direct run-test-files command) the sealed rule applies (no summary line -> 'summary line absent'). Line shapes and producers (plan, signalled batch, relay prefix) live beside TEST_FILE_LINE in run-test-files.js. (1) batch ended by a signal (OOM SIGKILL) under keep-going: the classified runner now writes '# test-files batch ended by SIGKILL: n file(s) may have no verdict' and its files are uncovered -> incomplete. (2) batch killed during its retry, after its summary: the signalled-batch line alone -> 'ended by SIGKILL'. (3) manifest timeout kill (SIGTERM) and (4) ENOBUFS (spawnSync kills with SIGTERM, stdout truncated): command.signal, usually also a plan deficit.
